beats.text: If you take home twenty thousand dollars a year, you're richer than nine in ten people on Earth.
Researchers lined up everyone's income, after tax and adjusted for prices.
Each bar is one tenth of humanity, from poorest to richest.
The person right in the middle lives on about three thousand four hundred dollars a year.
Twenty thousand puts you in the top tenth. In Germany or the US, more than half of people are there.
Feeling average at home can mean rich on Earth.

sources: van Teutem & Hasell (2025), Global inequality is huge – but so is the opportunity for people in high-income countries to support poor people, Our World in Data (25 Aug 2025), based on World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform – 'For a one-person household, an annual post-tax income of $20,000 already puts you in the richest tenth of the world'; 'That income bracket captures more than half the population in rich countries, like the Netherlands, the US, or Germany'; global median income ≈ 3,400 international dollars per year (2021 prices, 2025). Bars 1–8 schematic.
